focus: Pricing every hook gate: measured checker costs, fixed overhead, and the re-mint engines
noveltyJustification: 4 of 5 findings are new measurements and 1 extends an iteration-1 finding with its time dimension.
keyQuestions: Which git hook checks under `.skilled/scripts/git-hooks/` can move to CI or narrow to changed paths, and how much wall clock per commit and push does each cost?
ruledOut: Timing the full pre-commit end to end (four gates rewrite the index)
Treating hook latency as the primary time sink

graphEvents.label: Hook path is two orders of magnitude below CI run time

label: No pre-commit gate measured above a quarter second: mirror-sync 0.12 s over 91 mirror files, card sync 0.12 s, route guard 0.07 s, comment hygiene 0.20 s over 40 files.
Fixed hook overhead is small: a bounded git call costs about 20 ms and a bare Node spawn 0.02 s, so a typical commit pays an estimated one to two seconds of process startup.
The only unpriced commit-path term is the four re-mint engines, two of whose entry points contain write calls and therefore cannot be timed in a read-only research run.
pre-push is already lean: four bounded git calls, a 0.07 s routing guard, and the 40 s of report-only test suites already removed, so a push costs about a second.

Hook time is not the operator wait: CI means are 60 to 600 s against a 1-2 s commit, so a workflow cut saves minutes where a hook cut saves a second, and the iteration-1 duplication is maintenance debt rather than time debt.

direction: Deleting pre-commit gates to shorten the commit path
reason: Every measured gate is under 0.25 s, so a cut saves less than a second and can only lose a check.
